$comment: One entry per required behaviour (#71, FR-008). scripts/suite-selftest.mjs applies each
to a COPY of the repo, runs the suite, and asserts the NAMED test goes red.
`arm` names which assertion of a multi-arm behaviour this mutation is expected to red.
SC-014 is identity AND zero-<style>; SC-015 is three arms. One mutation cannot red them
all while staying collateral-clean, which is why guard 7 is a superset relation and not
set equality.
TWO ENTRIES ARE DELIBERATELY NOT THE OBVIOUS FORM, and the spec pins both:
SC-015 is NOT 'replace define with an empty function' — that unregisters sk-stub and
reds every other elements-owned test, failing the collateral bound on the mission's own
canonical mutation.
SC-014 is NOT 'hand-author a new CSSStyleSheet()' — the generated module already exports
exactly that and Lit adopts it by reference, so identity survives and the test stays
`subject` (#73) names the test FILE whose [id] must go red. Behaviour ids are no longer
unique across the suite — sk-nav-pill and the synthetic fixture both carry SC-006 — so an
id-only match would let a mutation red the fixture's test and be credited for the
element's. Guard 7 now compares (id, subject) pairs against behaviours.json's subjects.

#77 adds two for <sk-grid>, one per registry id it claims. Both mutate the ELEMENT rather than the test: dropping part="grid" must red the [SC-013] test, and emptying `static styles` must red [SC-014]. Note the SC-014 arm empties the array rather than swapping in a fresh CSSStyleSheet the way sk-stub's does — sk-grid.test.ts asserts adoptedStyleSheets.length, so both spellings red it, and the empty form also proves the length arm is load-bearing.

#77 adds two more for <sk-section-banner>. The SC-013 arm drops a part= attribute from a node the test targets by name; note it picks the DOT rather than the outermost part, because the outermost one is also a node the test queries to prove the element rendered at all, so removing it would red the test for the wrong reason.

#77's pre-merge gate added a SECOND SC-014 arm per element. The first arm empties `static styles`, which reds the `adoptedStyleSheets.length` assertion FIRST — vitest aborts there, so the identity assertion on the next line was never shown to be load-bearing, in the behaviour whose id is literally about identity. Swapping in a fresh CSSStyleSheet keeps length at 1 and can only red the identity arm. Both spellings are kept: one proves the length assertion, the other proves the identity assertion, and neither alone proves both.

#78 adds SIX: three for <sk-feature-card> and three for <sk-ribbon-card>. the SC-013 arm drops the CHIP's part rather than the card's, because the card part is also the node several other tests query to prove the element rendered at all. Both SC-014 spellings are carried FOR BOTH, per #77's finding that emptying the array reds the LENGTH assertion first and never exercises the identity one. An earlier revision of this PR carried both for feature-card and only the identity arm for ribbon-card, while this sentence claimed otherwise — three pre-merge lenses caught the asymmetry between the rule and its application.

#79 adds nine: three per component. sk-button's SC-013 arm drops the part from the ANCHOR branch, and was SEMANTICALLY INERT when first written — the [SC-013] test mounted without href, so it rendered the button branch and never saw the mutation. The harness said so and the test now exercises both branches, which is what a part rendered by two code paths needs. The check-bullet SC-013 arm drops the ICON's part rather than the bullet's, because the bullet part is also the node other tests query to prove the element rendered.

#140's pre-merge fold added two regression tests and then REMOVED the two mutations written for them. That was the right call, recorded so it is not retried — but an earlier revision of this note got the REASON wrong, and a lens corrected it. The wrong reason was 'this file holds one entry per required behaviour', which is false of this very file: 64 mutations cover 14 applicable behaviours, 16 of them carrying SC-014 and 14 carrying SC-013. The constraints that actually forbid these two entries are (a) guard 7 in scripts/suite-selftest.mjs, which keys on the `${id}@${subject}` PAIR and rejects any mutation naming a pair behaviours.json does not declare, so a mutation for a non-ADR-11 behaviour cannot be added without extending behaviours.json; and (b) guard 4, which requires the test that goes red to carry a [SC-NNN] marker — which these two deliberately do not. Binding them to SC-014 therefore reported 'semantically inert', correctly, since SC-014 is about style adoption. Marking the tests [SC-014] would be mislabelling; minting new ids would extend ADR-11's behaviour set, which #67 owns.

The two arms' red-first was demonstrated by DIRECT PROBE instead, and the measured output is recorded here because an earlier revision pointed a future maintainer at failure output that had never been written down anywhere. Reverting sk-button.ts to `href === undefined` gives: "removing href should revert to a <button>: expected 'A' to be 'BUTTON'". Reverting the tick in sk-check-bullet.css to `--sk-color-green` gives: "the tick in light mode is 1.73:1 (rgb(143, 203, 143) on rgb(248, 245, 236)) - AA needs 4.5". Dropping `.sk-light` from the light selector in tokens.css trips the shared theme guard in fixtures/.../contrast.ts: "the themes did not resolve different surfaces - dark=rgb(13, 14, 17), light=rgb(13, 14, 17)".

#78 adds three for <sk-blog-card>, and two are specific to the composition ruling: dropping sk-card's sheet reds the two-sheet identity assertion (and is the realistic regression — someone 'tidying' an import), and SWAPPING THE ORDER reds it too. That arm guards a CONVENTION rather than a current behaviour: the two sheets contest zero declarations, so a swap changes no computed style and the arm reds the structural identity-at-index assertion. An earlier revision of this note said order 'decides whose rules win where the two sheets touch', which was not true when written — two lenses caught it. The arm is kept because the moment either sheet grows a declaration the other sets, the order is what decides it. Neither is expressible for any other component in the repo.

#78's gate asked for a fourth blog-card arm dropping one `::slotted(` branch, and it is deliberately NOT added, for the reason #140 recorded above: guard 7 keys on a declared (id, subject) pair and guard 4 requires the red test to carry a [SC-NNN] marker. The arm that asserts slotted reach is a regression test, not an ADR-11 required behaviour, so binding it to SC-013 or SC-014 would mislabel it and minting an id would extend ADR-11, which #67 owns. The coverage is real either way and is doubled: the fixture asserts a computed style off a slotted node AND that the hover rule survives parsing, and check-adopted-css-boundaries now rejects `::slotted(x):hover` outright with three committed probes.

#77 adds THREE for <sk-site-footer>. The SC-013 arm drops the DIVIDER's part rather than the footer's, because the footer part is also the node other tests query to prove the element rendered at all — the same reasoning check-bullet's arm records. Both SC-014 spellings are carried, per #77's own earlier finding: emptying the array reds the adoptedStyleSheets.length assertion FIRST and vitest aborts there, so the identity assertion on the next line is never shown to be load-bearing in the behaviour whose id is literally about identity. Swapping in a fresh CSSStyleSheet keeps length at 1 and can only red the identity arm.

#77's pass-2 gate asked for a FOURTH site-footer arm covering the conditional divider, and it was written, bound to SC-013, and then REMOVED — the harness correctly reported it 'semantically inert'. Forcing the divider to always render does not break SC-013, which is 'every declared part is targetable': the part is still present and still targetable. The conditionality is a regression guard, not an ADR-11 required behaviour, so it has no (id, subject) pair to bind to and guard 4 has no [SC-NNN]-marked test to red. Third time this programme has reached that boundary (#140, #143, here), and the answer is the same each time: the coverage is real — `the divider is drawn only when there is a legal line to divide` asserts absence, whitespace-only, and the property arriving later — it is simply held by a test rather than by the harness. Minting an id would extend ADR-11's behaviour set, which #67 owns.

#182 adds two for <sk-page-header>, one per axis, and both mutate the ELEMENT rather than the test. Each flips `reflect: true` to `reflect: false` on one of the two new reactive properties; the named [SC-010] test asserts the pre-upgrade value reaches the ATTRIBUTE, so each arm reds it on its own. The sticky arm is not merely a reflection check: the sticky geometry is expressed as `:host([sticky])` — it HAS to be on the host, because an inner box's containing block is the host and it cannot move inside it (measured) — so an unreflected `sticky` is a sticky axis that silently does nothing. NO THIRD ARM FOR THE REFLOW THRESHOLD, and that is a stated gap rather than an omission: guard 7 requires every mutation's (id, subject) pair to be declared in behaviours.json, and tests/node/config-contract.test.ts asserts that file's applicable id set equals ADR-11's list exactly. ADR-11 has no id for a responsive/threshold behaviour, so the drop blocks are covered by ordinary tests here and by apps/storybook/src/tests/sk-page-header-sticky.spec.ts, and the registry gap is filed as an issue rather than closed by mis-filing a layout assertion under a reflection id.

#146 WP01 adds ELEVEN arms: one part removal and two independent style-adoption arms for each of three primitives, plus one late-upgrade property-registration removal each for status tone and entity label. Section-header is slot-only and does not claim SC-010.

#146 WP02 adds SEVEN sk-action-row arms: duplicate dispatch, wrong detail, false bubbling/composed flags, pre-upgrade rowId registration loss, one non-root part removal, empty styles, and fresh-sheet identity. There is no cancellation arm because SC-009 is inapplicable.

#146 WP03 adds ONE generated react-action-row arm that removes the wrapper listener inside the harness copy. The four element subjects contribute 18 mission arms and this wrapper contributes the nineteenth.

#177 adds TWO for <sk-card>, one per id it now claims, and both mutate the ELEMENT rather than the test. The SC-013 arm replaces the status fail-open branch with a THROW — the exact regression sk-card.markup.ts records at length, and the only mutation in this file whose red is the ABSENCE of a part rather than a wrong value: Lit rejects updateComplete, render() returns no tree, and `[part="card"]` is not in the shadow root to target. That is why the [SC-013] test mounts BOTH a plain and an unknown-status card; with only the plain one it would have stayed green through the throw, which is the certifying-absence class this harness exists to catch. The SC-010 arm flips reflect on `status`: the named test asserts the pre-upgrade value reaches the ATTRIBUTE, so an unreflected status is an axis that does nothing outside the shadow root, and no static consumer or CSS author can see it. NO ARM FOR THE VOCABULARY ASSERTION, deliberately: guard 7 keys on a declared (id, subject) pair and guard 4 requires the red test to carry an [SC-NNN] marker, and there is no ADR-11 id for 'two components share one enum'. Binding it to SC-013 or SC-010 would mislabel it and minting an id would extend ADR-11's behaviour set, which #67 owns. The coverage is real either way — the test compares Object.keys(CARD_STATUSES) to STATUS_TONES by value and order — it is simply held by a test rather than by the harness. Fourth time this programme has reached that boundary (#140, #143, #77, here); the answer has been the same each time.

#147 WP03 adds exactly two SC-013 arms, one per newly recorded subject. Each removes a non-root part from the authored element inside the harness copy and must red the existing all-parts fixture assertion without creating a new behaviour id or SC-014 pair. On the refreshed train after #177, total mutations move 132 -> 134.

#178 adds TWELVE arms for <sk-notice>, all mutating the ELEMENT. Three need their reason recorded.
TWO SC-010 ARMS. The first flips `reflect` on `tone` — the ordinary property-before-upgrade arm. The SECOND deletes `message` from `static properties` and is the arm this mission exists for: it reproduces the defect sk-form-input.ts records twice. Measured red: `expected 'Retrying in 5s' to contain 'Retrying in 2s'` — a STALE MESSAGE. It also reds the UNMARKED re-announcement test, which costs nothing because isBehaviourTest keys on the [SC-NNN] marker, so an unmarked test is invisible to the collateral bound. That is how the announcement contract gets harness coverage without minting an id ADR-11 does not have.
THE FIRST expectCollateral IN THIS FILE, on the SC-012 arm. Deleting `this.focus()` reds [SC-012] AND the uncancelled contrast branch of [SC-009] — a property of the DESIGN, not of test hygiene: the element does not remove itself, so the only default action a cancelable dismiss can prevent is the focus move, which makes focus the one behaviour those two ids share. Guard 5 inverts on the flag and requires the collateral to occur, so it asserts rather than exempts. The [SC-012] assertion had to be moved INSIDE the shadow root first: CI measured the arm 'semantically inert' against the original `document.activeElement === element`, which holds whether or not focus moves, because focus on a node inside a shadow root already reports the host.
SC-013 drops the CONTENT part, not the root `notice` part (the node other tests query to prove the element rendered) and not `marker` (which [SC-011] reads aria-hidden from). Both SC-014 spellings are carried, per #77's finding.

#216 KEEPS the vocabulary assertion this file's #177 note describes, and adds NO arm. The first revision of this entry said the assertion had been removed because a fork was "no longer REPRESENTABLE"; that was measurably false and a pre-merge reviewer falsified it in one edit. What #216 removed is one SHAPE of fork — two authored lists that can drift apart. CARD_STATUSES is now Object.fromEntries(STATUS_TONES.map(...)), so there is no second list. But the derivation is an EXPRESSION and nothing gates the expression: appending ['rogue','sk-card--status-rogue'] inside the fromEntries argument keeps the index-signature type, so the cast stays clean, typecheck-all passes for five projects, build-element-markup regenerates and WRITES SkCardStatusRogueHTML with a class in no stylesheet, and check-adopted-css-boundaries, check-element-css-hygiene, check-no-css-in-source, check-elements-entries, check-manifest-content, check-part-ratchet and htmlhint all stay green. The order-sensitive equality in fixtures/elements-behaviour/src/sk-card.test.ts is the only thing that reds, and it is verified to red on exactly that edit. Note the sibling BEM-family test CANNOT stand in for it: it derives its expectation from the key under test, so it is self-fulfilling for any key, 'rogue' included. So the boundary the #177 note named — a real claim with no ADR-11 id, the fourth time (#140, #143, #77, #177) — is UNCHANGED and still held by an ordinary test rather than by this harness. The count is unchanged for the same reason it was then: guard 7 keys on a declared (id, subject) pair and guard 4 requires an [SC-NNN] marker, and there is still no id for 'the expression that derives one component's map from another's vocabulary'.

#148 WP03 adds NINE bar-chart arms: seven element arms cover duplicate dispatch, exact detail, bubbling/composed flags, property-only series registration, label part exposure, and the independent stylesheet length and identity contracts; two React arms cover the generated listener and property bridge.

#196 AND #204 ADD TWO IDS AND THIS FILE IS WHERE THE COST SHOWS. THREE CHANGES, none of them additive-only.
(1) SC-016 (delegate/rendered-control correspondence) is carried by the arm that was already here as SC-003 'probe type assigned before value' — RE-KEYED, not duplicated. ADR-14 calls that defect 'the clearest instance' of the two sources disagreeing, so it was always a correspondence arm; it was filed under SC-003 because no other id existed. SC-003 keeps eleven arms and its own tests, so nothing is left uncovered by the move.
(2) The SC-013 arm 'constraint attribute reaches the inner control' is RE-SITED from `pattern=${nothing}` to `inputmode=${nothing}`. Measured, not assumed: dropping `pattern` from the rendered control reds the [SC-013] forwarding test AND the [SC-016] correspondence test, because with item 10 in force it IS a correspondence defect — the probe still holds the constraint the control lost. `inputmode` reaches no validity at all, so the arm reds the forwarding test alone. The [SC-013] test asserts six forwarded attributes and the arm drops one of them either way, and the `pattern` case is not left unwatched: it is measured red by the [SC-016] test.
WHY NOT expectCollateral: it would have removed guard 5's blast-radius bound from three surgical arms (the merged-flag loop, the probe value sync, and this one) to make room for one new id. Naming both ids on the shared test does the same work without weakening anything, and `[SC-002][SC-003] a readonly control still submits` is the precedent for a dual-marked test in this very file.
(3) SC-017 (responsive threshold) gets TWO arms, one per documented threshold, and both mutate the GENERATED packages/elements/src/page-header/sk-page-header.css.js. That is forced rather than chosen: the test job never builds, so an arm against the authored packages/styles/src/page-header/sk-page-header.css would be semantically inert — SC-010's arm against generated packages/react/src/SkTransitionMatrix.js is the precedent for mutating a generated artefact. The HEIGHT arm reds ONE test where the WIDTH arm reds two, and that asymmetry is the measurement #182 wrote two separate @media blocks to obtain: only the width threshold is reachable live at the lane's 414px viewport, so the height block is falsifiable only through the sheet-reading assertion, and joining the two conditions would make it unfalsifiable altogether.
